{{Quote|Manaan's an unusual place. Not for its water, mind you&hellip; it's the kolto. Healing juice. Only place where it occurs in the galaxy.|[[Jolee Bindo]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />}}
'''Kolto''' was a liquid known for its healing abilities. It was found in the [[Water/Legends|water]] of the [[Ocean/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], with a significant concentration near the [[Hrakert Rift]] along with other underwater chasms. It was considered a valuable commodity during the [[Jedi Civil War]], but its significance was lost over time, being replaced in favor of [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], kolto was considered less effective than bacta.

==History==
Kolto was a liquid that could only be found naturally in the depths of the [[Ocean/Legends|oceanic]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Manaan/Legends|Manaan]], and it was known for its healing capabilities. Both the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith]] and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] had an equally limited supply of kolto during the [[Jedi Civil War]], so they sought a way to get more of it to gain an advantage, but all attempts to synthesize kolto failed.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> In turn, it became a vital export for the economy of Manaan and for the [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that controlled the planet.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /><ref name="Manaan: Depths of History">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040205manaan|text=Manaan: Depths of History|int=Manaan: Depths of History}}</ref>

The [[Hrakert Rift]] was considered a prime location for kolto harvesting during the Jedi Civil War, being home to a giant [[Firaxan shark/Legends|firaxan shark]] known as the [[Progenitor]], which may have been guarding the kolto. According to Selkath legend, kolto was also produced by the Progenitor. However, the scientists [[Kono Nolan]] and [[Sami (Human)|Sami]] believed that the shark had reached its large size and old age because it was feeding on the kolto.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

During the Jedi Civil War, the Selkath remained neutral, favoring neither the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] nor the Sith Empire. As a result, both governments set up "equal" operations on Manaan. Desperate for the healing power of kolto and to get an advantage over the Sith, Republic emissaries crafted a deal with several key members of the Selkath government. Fearing that the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] would destroy the Selkath society, these leaders allowed the Republic to construct a secret [[Water/Legends|underwater]] facility in the Rift to harvest kolto.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" />

[[File:Progenitor-KOTOR.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The [[Progenitor]], which was believed to have been a possible source of kolto]]
During the time between the Jedi Civil War and the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the production of kolto suffered substantially and the value escalated. With the cost of kolto so high, the market for it collapsed in favor of a less expensive alternative: [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]].<ref name="Manaan: Depths of History" /> The reason for the sharp decline of kolto production was hotly contested in academic circles. Nevertheless, the economy of Manaan collapsed and kolto became almost completely forgotten.<ref name="Manaan: Depths of History" /><ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref>

With the onset of the Galactic Civil War, bacta had become the primary healing agent used in medicine. Aware of kolto's presence on Manaan and historical significance, [[Palpatine/Legends|Emperor Palpatine]] invaded Manaan and enslaved the native Selkath.<ref name="Manaan: Depths of History" /> The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] exploited the Selkath and possibly their kolto resources. While kolto was still being used during the Galactic Civil War, it did not possess great value. It appeared to be less effective than bacta, but was used as a cheaper alternative.<ref name="Darth Bane: Path of Destruction" /><ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref> In their research, however, some historians noted that kolto may have been more effective in the past.<ref name="Manaan: Depths of History" /> By [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], kolto was in use aboard the [[Imperial prison barge]] [[Purge (prison barge)|''Purge'']], where it was administered to some medical patients.<ref name="DT">''[[Death Troopers]]''</ref>

==Usage==
[[File:Kolto_tank.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A kolto tank]]
{{Quote|Kolto for your cuts.|A military phrase referring to in-field medical care|<ref name="The Old Republic: Deceived">''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref>}}
Kolto was most commonly applied through complete submersion in a kolto tank. Patients would remain inside the tank, submerged in a solution of kolto, until their wounds were healed. During its peak, kolto tanks were aboard Republic starships, inside government buildings and in medical facilities. The concentration of kolto could be tailored to the patient, allowing the input of different solutions.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

Kolto was also one of the primary components of [[Medpac/Legends|medpacs]] during the Jedi Civil War.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> Medpacs contained small amounts of the liquid for easy carriage and transport. Therefore, the amount of kolto was usually not substantial, so medpacs functioned primarily as first-aid supplements.<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /><ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords" />

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], both the frequency of kolto usage and the diversity of delivery methods expanded, particularly among the elite ranks of the Republic and [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]]. While regular troops and civilians on both sides relied regularly on standard kolto tanks and medpacs, [[Imperial Agent]] Operatives delivered kolto injections via wrist-mounted dart launchers or hovering medical probes in support of their comrades. Even the likes of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] modified their missiles to saturate small areas with revitalizing kolto mist.

Both factions also explored alternatives and supplements to kolto, including using narcotics such as [[Spice/Legends|spice]] in place of painkillers.

==Behind the scenes==
Kolto first appeared in ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released by [[BioWare]] during the summer of [[2003]]. In the game, the player is given a choice of two possible outcomes: player can pressurize the fuel tanks to four million sangens, resulting in detonation of the fuel supply, which destroys the internal mechanisms and appeases the Progenitor; kolto production would then resume. As a non-canon option, player can kill the Progenitor, which results in the cessation of kolto production (the poison that kills the Progenitor also corrupts the kolto, turning it black), spikes in kolto prices, and the banning of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] permanently from Manaan.

Both kolto and Manaan itself also appear in ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', where infantry units can get a healing bonus due to the presence of kolto. Kolto, however, is not mentioned anywhere else after the [[Old Republic era]], not having been conceived before ''Knights of the Old Republic''.

Comments from ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'' support the theory that kolto was an inferior healing agent to bacta. It mentions that miners who couldn't afford bacta used kolto as a cheaper alternative. This could be circumstantial, however, as kolto may have already lost its economic significance in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] economy.

Kolto is used frequently in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', the [[Wikipedia:massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] released by [[BioWare]] in December of [[2011]]. It is utilized by all of the non-[[The Force/Legends|Force]]-using player character classes that have access to healing-type abilities.
